CR_STEPS|/prep/points/1: dense and smooth mineral substrates must be roughened (sand, high-pressure water or shot blasting)
CR_STEPS|/derust/short: Exposed steel is de-rusted completely, to cleanliness level SA 2.5, free of dust and grease.
CR_STEPS|/derust/overview: The exposed reinforcing steels must be totally de-rusted and must be clear of dust and grease up to the standard cleanliness level SA 2.5 by suitable measures.
CR_STEPS|/derust/points/0: blast all around the bar, also behind it
CR_STEPS|/derust/points/1: exposed reinforcing steels must be pretreated with the corrosion protection {HSF}
CR_STEPS|/protect/title: Coat the reinforcement twice with ASOCRET-HS-FLEX
CR_STEPS|/protect/short: Two brush coats, fully covering; the second after approx. 2 hours.
CR_STEPS|/protect/overview: {HSF} is applied to the reinforcing steel with a brush in two application steps, ensuring full covering.
CR_STEPS|/protect/points/0: water addition for corrosion protection: approx. 5.5–5.75 l per 25 kg
CR_STEPS|/protect/points/1: mixing time ca. 3 minutes; mix again after an activation time of 5 minutes
CR_STEPS|/protect/points/2: the second coat is applied after approx. 2 hours waiting time, when the first coat is brushable
CR_STEPS|/protect/points/3: consumption approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm layer thickness; approx. 1 mm per application step
CR_STEPS|/protect/warning: The repair mortar {BIS540} can be applied approx. 6 hours after the second coat has hardened.
CR_STEPS|/wet/short: Dampen 24 hours and 2 hours before; matt damp at the time of application.
CR_STEPS|/wet/overview: Dampen the pre-treated mineral substrate sufficiently 24 hours and 2 hours before application. Pre-moisten the dry mineral substrate so that it is matt damp at the time of application.
CR_STEPS|/wet/points/0: matt damp: no shiny film of water, no puddles
CR_STEPS|/wet/points/1: the bond coat and the mortar follow directly
CR_STEPS|/bond/title: Brush in the bond coat ASOCRET-HS-FLEX
CR_STEPS|/bond/short: One coat with a hard brush, down to the pores, fully covering.
CR_STEPS|/bond/overview: {HSF} is brushed into the prepared substrate with a hard broom in a single coat, down to the pores and such that it is full covering.
CR_STEPS|/bond/points/0: water addition for the bond coat: approx. 6.75–7.0 l per 25 kg
CR_STEPS|/bond/points/1: mixing time ca. 3 minutes; mix again after an activation time of 5 minutes
CR_STEPS|/bond/points/2: consumption approx. 1.5 kg/m² per mm layer thickness
CR_STEPS|/bond/warning: In case of interruptions or after hardening, the bond coat must set completely. Repeat the application including the bond coat after an appropriate waiting time.
CR_STEPS|/fill/title: Re-profile with ASOCRET-BIS-5/40, wet in wet
CR_STEPS|/fill/short: Into the fresh bond coat, compacted and levelled flush; up to 20 mm per step.
CR_STEPS|/fill/overview: The repair mortar {BIS540} is applied while the bond coat is still wet, in the required layer thickness. Then the mortar is compacted and levelled flush with the surface.
CR_STEPS|/fill/points/0: put approx. 2.8–3.0 l of water into a clean mixing bucket and mix with 25 kg of powder to a homogeneous, lump-free mass
CR_STEPS|/fill/points/2: add the remaining water (in total approx. 3.5–3.75 l) and mix sufficiently; use a forced paddle mixer for larger quantities
CR_STEPS|/fill/points/3: apply into the fresh bond coat, compact, level flush with the surface
CR_STEPS|/fill/points/4: with large surface applications the layer thickness can be up to max. 20 mm in one application step
CR_STEPS|/fill/points/5: for greater layer thicknesses a multiple layer application is recommended
CR_STEPS|/fill/warning: Do not add water or new mortar to mortar that has already set in order to make it workable again (risk of inadequate strength development).
CR_STEPS|/fill/note: Pot life approx. 60 minutes. Consumption approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm. Can be trowelled and sprayed; machine application: Technical Information No. 43.
CR_STEPS|/fine/short: Scratch coat first, then the layer, 1–6 mm; strike off within the pot life.
CR_STEPS|/fine/overview: On the prepared substrate, {BIS16} is applied beforehand with a scratch coat and then in the desired layer thickness. Striking off is done with a suitable tool (float, trowel) within the pot life.
CR_STEPS|/fine/points/0: water addition: 5–5.25 l per 25 kg; mixing time ca. 3 minutes; after a settling period of ca. 5 minutes homogenise again
CR_STEPS|/fine/points/1: up to 6 mm per application step
CR_STEPS|/fine/points/2: the surface can be treated with a felt or sponge board after a corresponding waiting time
CR_STEPS|/fine/points/3: consumption approx. 1.6 kg/m² per mm; pot life approx. 60 minutes
CR_STEPS|/fine/points/4: on {BIS540}: overcoat after 24 hours at the earliest
CR_STEPS|/cure/short: Protect from rapid drying; keep damp for at least 3–5 days.
CR_STEPS|/cure/overview: After application, the mortar surfaces must generally be protected from rapid drying using suitable measures: keep the surfaces damp for at least 3–5 days using water mist nozzles, wet jute sheets or by covering with film.
CR_STEPS|/cure/points/0: the film must be attached to the surfaces in such a way that an air exchange is ruled out
CR_STEPS|/cure/points/1: direct sunlight, draughts, high temperature fluctuations and low humidity need more attention
CR_STEPS|/cure/points/2: if a cementitious waterproofing slurry follows, it can be applied as an alternative curing method after approx. 24 hours
CR_STEPS|/clean/short: Rinse tools with water immediately. Store cool and dry.
CR_STEPS|/clean/overview: Rinse tools with water immediately after use.
CR_STEPS|/clean/points/0: storage: cool, dry, protected from sunlight
CR_STEPS|/clean/points/1: min. 12 months in the original container ({IM}: min. 18 months)
CR_STEPS|/wprep/short: Roughen dense surfaces; high-pressure water jetting; finish by cleaning with pressure water.
CR_STEPS|/wprep/overview: A load-bearing substrate is a precondition for a long-lasting bond. Less adhesive and bond-damaging substances must be completely removed.
CR_STEPS|/wprep/points/0: dense and smooth substrates must be roughened (sand, high-pressure water or shot blasting)
CR_STEPS|/wprep/points/1: high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar) and jets with fixed blasting agents are suitable
CR_STEPS|/wprep/points/2: the last application step must be cleaning with pressure water jetting
CR_STEPS|/wprep/points/3: requirement: firm, load-bearing, pore open, clean, absorbent
CR_STEPS|/wprep/points/4: pre-moisten to matt damp; the formation of puddles must be avoided
CR_STEPS|/plug/short: Running water is stopped first, with the plugging mortar FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T.
CR_STEPS|/plug/overview: Water ingress must be stopped in advance with FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T.
CR_STEPS|/plug/points/0: system “Retrospective concrete waterproofing”: mix the plugging mortar with approx. 25 % water to a pliable consistency, pot life approx. 3 minutes
CR_STEPS|/plug/points/1: press the plug into the leaking area and hold until it has hardened, then trowel the surface
CR_STEPS|/plug/note: Cracks that conduct water over their length are injected: see the guide “Crack sealing / injection resins”.
CR_STEPS|/chase/short: Approx. 20 mm wide and approx. 25 mm deep, U-shaped.
CR_STEPS|/chase/overview: Structural cracks are to be prised open up to a width of approx. 20 mm and a depth of approx. 25 mm.
CR_STEPS|/chase/points/1: U-shaped, not V-shaped: the mortar needs flanks to hold on to
CR_STEPS|/chase/points/2: consumption for this cross-section: approx. 1.3 kg {IM} per metre
CR_STEPS|/slurry/short: The crystalline slurry goes on first; the mortar follows wet in wet.
CR_STEPS|/slurry/overview: Screen the edges with {IC}. For coves: screen the substrate with {IC} and then apply {IM} wet in wet.
CR_STEPS|/slurry/points/1: {IC}: crystalline waterproofing slurry, penetrates the concrete via the capillaries
CR_STEPS|/im/title: Fill with ASOCRET-IM, form the cove
CR_STEPS|/im/short: Flush into the chased crack; coved fillet approx. 4 cm high, rounded.
CR_STEPS|/im/overview: Seal wet in wet with {IM} flush with the surface. For the cove, apply {IM} wet in wet into the fresh {IC} with an edge height of approx. 4 cm in a rounded form.
CR_STEPS|/im/points/0: water addition: 3.75–4.25 l per 25 kg, mix to a homogeneous, lump-free mass
CR_STEPS|/im/points/1: up to 10 mm per application step
CR_STEPS|/im/points/3: consumption approx. 1.7 kg/m² per mm; chased crack or coved fillet approx. 1.3 kg/m
CR_STEPS|/im/warning: Do not use on frozen substrates. {IM} cannot be used as an additive to concrete or plaster.
CR_STEPS|/ic/short: After approx. 1–3 hours the mortar is overcoated with the crystalline slurry.
CR_STEPS|/ic/overview: After approx. 1–3 hours, rework {IM} with {IC}. If this is not possible during this period, the surface should be roughened again after totally hardening and then coated with {IC}.
CR_STEPS|/ic/points/0: system “Retrospective concrete waterproofing”: two coats of {IC}, the second while the first is still tacky
CR_STEPS|/wcure/short: Protect against rapid water removal; keep damp for at least 3 days.
CR_STEPS|/wcure/overview: {IM} must be protected against rapid water removal using suitable protective measures.
CR_STEPS|/wcure/points/0: system “Retrospective concrete waterproofing”: protect from weathering, keep damp for a minimum of 3 days, first dampening after approx. 1 day
CR_STEPS|/wcure/points/1: the reaction with the free lime in the concrete can result in slight efflorescence: not a defect, it can be brushed off
CR_STEPS|/wcure/points/2: different colouring depends on the different moisture content in the concrete
CRS_T|/steel/problem: The cover has carbonated or taken up chlorides, the bar rusts, the rust needs more room than the steel and blows the cover off. Rust stains, cracks along the bar, exposed reinforcement.
CRS_T|/steel/solution: The full system: break out to sound concrete, de-rust the bar to SA 2.5, two coats of {HSF} as corrosion protection, {HSF} as bond coat, {BIS540} wet in wet, {BIS16} as the fine finish.
CRS_T|/breakout/problem: Mechanical damage, poorly compacted zones or broken edges, 5–40 mm deep. The reinforcement is still covered.
CRS_T|/breakout/solution: Prepare the substrate, pre-wet, brush in the bond coat {HSF} and re-profile wet in wet with the non-slump repair mortar {BIS540}; {BIS16} closes the surface.
CRS_T|/surface/problem: Pores, blowholes and unevenness up to 6 mm, on walls, ceilings and floors; pool tank walls that have to be levelled before waterproofing.
CRS_T|/surface/solution: {BIS16}: a scratch coat into the matt damp substrate, then the layer of 1–6 mm, struck off within the pot life and finished with a felt or sponge board.
CRS_T|/water/problem: Water comes through cracks, tie holes or the wall–floor joint of a concrete structure, also against negative water pressure.
CRS_T|/water/solution: Stop running water with FIX 10-S or FIX 20-T, chase the crack to 20 × 25 mm, screen with the crystalline slurry {IC} and fill wet in wet with {IM}; coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the wall–floor joint; overcoat with {IC} after 1–3 hours.
CRS_T|/layers/corr/1: on the de-rusted reinforcement, two brush coats
CRS_T|/layers/corr/4: second coat after approx. 2 h; mortar approx. 6 h after the second coat
CRS_T|/layers/bond/1: brushed into the matt damp substrate, one coat, down to the pores
CRS_T|/layers/fill/2: 5–40 mm, up to 20 mm per step
CRS_T|/layers/fine/1: closes the surface, felt or sponge finish
CRS_T|/layers/scratch/1: the same mortar, pressed into the matt damp substrate
CRS_T|/layers/ic1/1: screens the flanks and the cove substrate
CRS_T|/layers/im/1: fills the chased crack flush; coved fillet approx. 4 cm
CRS_T|/layers/im/3: approx. 1.3 kg/m (crack, cove); 1.7 kg/m² per mm
CRS_T|/layers/ic2/1: over the mortar and the surface
WPT|/wp.kicker: Waterproofing and Restoration · Waterproofing materials – mineral-based
WPT|/wp.title: Mineral-based waterproofing
WPT|/wp.sub: Cementitious slurries and flexible thick-layer coatings, applied as one system.
WPT|/wp.intro: The rigid slurries {AQ1K} and {AQ1KP} for substrates that are not prone to cracking, the crack-bridging slurry {AQ2K}, the rapid flexible coating {RB400} for pressing water and radon, and the OS 5b surface protection {OS} for car park decks. Mineral, watertight, vapour permeable — applied by brush, trowel or spray.
WPT|/wp.photoCap: System build-up: substrate levelled, sealing cove installed, two coats of waterproofing, detail sealed, protected.
WPT|/wp.stats/0/3: {RB400} after PG MDS/FPD: 2 mm; ASTM C836 > 3 mm
WPT|/wp.stats/1/3: {RB400} at 3.0 mm dry film thickness; {AQ2K} 2.5 bar; {AQ1K} 1 bar
WPT|/wp.stats/2/3: all slurries against pressing water from the rear, WTA datasheet 4-6
WPT|/wp.stats/3/3: {AQ1KP}: recoatable after approx. 90 minutes — even under unfavourable conditions
